text: [excited] Parts of America's air traffic control... still run on floppy disks.
[curious] Passengers stream movies at thirty thousand feet.
But down in the control rooms, four systems from the nineteen-eighties are still on duty.
[surprised] When a part breaks, the spare can come from eBay.
[amused] Some towers still hand around little paper strips, one for every flight.
[dramatically] And one floppy disk holds one point four four megabytes.
[mischievously] That's smaller than a single selfie.
[deadpan] Luckily, the old machines still work.
[deadpan] Unluckily, almost nobody makes the disks anymore.
[curious] So why not just swap them? Because air traffic never stops.
[playfully] It's like changing the tyres on a car... while it's driving down the highway. Full of passengers.
[confident] This week, the F.A.A. finally posted it, with emojis: floppy disks from the eighties, out. Twenty-first century tech, in.
One new screen will show weather, outages and alerts together, at four hundred and thirty-five sites by twenty twenty-eight.
[amused] For most of us, a floppy disk is just the little save icon.
[whispers] Turns out, for air traffic... it was the actual save button.
